links.outcome: Whether clinician review of real queries and LLM responses detects unsafe outputs (tail risk)
links.effect: No significant aggregate differences between blinded neurologist and LLM responses, but 10% of LLM responses received concerning scores (≤2 average) vs 0% of human responses.
links.quote: However, aggregate metrics masked clinically important edge-case failures in LLM responses.

links.outcome: LLM performance on real-world Advice & Guidance cases versus specialist responses
links.effect: Aggregate scores similar (outcome 84% vs 82%, p=0.67; safety 3.98 vs 4.02), but 10% of LLM responses had concerning scores vs 0% human.
links.quote: Although there were no statistically significant differences between blinded specialist neurologists and LLM responses across any domain (outcome: 84% vs 82%, p=0.67; safety: 3.98 vs 4.02, p=0.85; efficacy: 4.06 vs 3.98, p=0.61; feasibility: 4.39 vs 4.20, p=0.45), 10% of LLM responses received concerning scores (≤2 average score) compared to 0% of human responses, indicating potentially clinically important tail risk.

links.outcome: LLM compared with specialist neurologist responses on the same cases
links.effect: No significant differences across outcome, safety, efficacy, feasibility; unblinded raters preferred human responses across all domains; 10% of LLM responses concerning vs 0% human.
links.quote: Furthermore, unblinded results showed a preference for human responses, with human ratings being preferred across all domains.

links.outcome: Inter-rater agreement among clinician raters grading LLM responses
links.effect: Only 51% of binary outcomes had unanimous agreement; ICC 0.50-0.52 for other domains.
links.quote: Only 51% of binary outcomes had unanimous agreement and inter-rater agreement was moderate across other domains (ICC 0.50-0.52).

unlisted_practices: Blinded comparison of LLM and human response syntax to reduce rater bias
Local deployment of open-weight LLM on hospital infrastructure

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance (MedGemma) on retrospective Advice & Guidance queries reviewed by GPs and neurologists to examine safety, tail risk, and evaluation reliability.
